statement: The two-toggle collaboration enablement (ADR-065) shipped on 2026-09-06 as a Genesis-only change with no migration, moving the platform from v0.66.0 to v0.66.1.
scope: As-built record of the v0.66.x collaboration enablement release.

statement: ADR-063 had originally delivered collaboration as a single environment-only opt-in controlled by one variable.
scope: Background motivating ADR-065's richer enablement model.

statement: The user asked for an in-app Settings toggle to turn collaboration on or off, guarded so it can be enabled only when the Genesis Hub app is reachable in the dev environment (so nothing breaks).
The user required collaboration to be active only when both the environment master switch and the in-app Settings toggle are on.
The user required the Hub URL to come from the dev-tagged environment, paired with a one-time static Hub app UUID.
Collaboration UI config is persisted by CollabConfigStore to a JSON file written atomically; it holds the toggle state (default off) and the Hub app UUID, and requires no database migration.
scope: Persistence contract for the Settings-level collaboration toggle.

statement: Collaboration counts as enabled only when both toggles are on: the service considers itself enabled only if a provider was built at boot (the env master) and the UI toggle in the config file is on.
scope: Gate for whether collaboration is active; both conditions are required.

statement: Every publish and pull is gated through the service's require-enabled check, so flipping the Settings toggle takes effect immediately without restarting the app.
scope: Runtime effect of the Settings toggle.

statement: Helpers were added to report whether the env master configured a Hub and to resolve the Hub app UUID, where the stored config value takes precedence over the environment-variable fallback; the resolved UUID drives KB exclusion of the Hub app itself.
scope: Hub-app UUID resolution precedence and its KB exclusion effect.

statement: When building the Appian sync provider, the Hub base URL is derived from the dev environment's URL plus the standard Appian Web-API mount; a configured Hub URL serves only as the fallback when there is no dev environment, and a base_url property was added to the provider for status display.
scope: How the Appian Hub base URL is resolved.

statement: An availability endpoint reports whether the env master is enabled and whether the provider's meta ping succeeds, combining these into whether collaboration can be enabled.
Setting the collaboration config (UI toggle and Hub app UUID) is rejected with a 409 unless the env master is on and the Hub is reachable.
scope: Guard on the config-write API; the 409 is returned when preconditions are not met.

statement: The read config endpoint was extended to return the overall enabled flag, the env flag, the UI toggle, availability, the Hub app UUID and the Hub URL.
scope: Fields returned by the collaboration config read API.

statement: The Settings Collaboration screen shows a switch (disabled with an explanatory reason when the env master is off or the Hub is unreachable) and a one-time Hub-app-UUID field, backed by new availability and set-config hooks and API client methods; stale copy about being wired later was removed.
scope: Settings web surface for the collaboration toggle.

statement: In v0.66.0 the bare dev-environment root was used as the Hub base URL, but the Appian provider expects the Web-API prefix, so the meta endpoint was never reached and availability was always false with a null Hub URL; the fix appended the Web-API mount during base-URL resolution, with a test asserting the derived prefix.
scope: Lesson: an Appian Hub base URL must include the Web-API mount or availability checks silently fail.

statement: v0.66.1 passed its gates (backend tests, lint, web tsc/eslint/vitest and build, plus phase 35/37/38 acceptance) and was verified live against a dev environment with collaboration fully enabled and reporting all flags true.

Turning on the env master still requires restarting serve with the collaboration-enabled and Appian-provider environment variables set (the deployment-level switch), whereas the Settings toggle is the runtime control.
scope: The env master is set at deployment via restart; the Settings toggle operates at runtime.

statement: A configured Hub URL remains only a fallback, used solely for a deployment that has no dev-tagged environment.
scope: When the static Hub URL fallback applies.

statement: The first real publish of a completed feature stage to the live Hub (v0.66.2) failed with a 400 reporting an invalid kind or missing sync UUID.
scope: Incident that exposed the stage_artifact contract mismatch.

statement: The stage entity binding had sent the wrong Hub shape: a feature_stage kind, a feature sync-uuid parent, and an artifact blob keyed by the stage's own sync uuid.
scope: Describes the incorrect publish shape later corrected to the frozen contract.

statement: The frozen Hub contract represents a stage as a stage_artifact record carrying a parent sync uuid and parent kind, a renamed upstream-versions field, and an artifact blob keyed by parent-sync-uuid and stage with that blob key stored on the record.
scope: Frozen Hub contract shape for stage artifacts (per spec 36-01 §2.1).

statement: The permissive local Hub emulator accepted the wrong record shape, so all phase-38 tests and acceptance passed and the mismatch surfaced only on the live Appian call.
scope: Lesson: a permissive emulator can hide contract violations that only a real Hub rejects.

statement: The fix remapped the stage binding (setting kind, parent kind, an outbound rename, and a blob key plus content hash on the record, with pull reversing the rename and fetching the blob by parent-and-stage key), updated the SDLC tests to the contract shape, and added a guard test that every binding kind is a real contract record kind.
scope: Remediation for the stage_artifact mismatch, including a guard test for binding kinds.

statement: v0.66.2 was verified live by publishing a feature stage as a stage_artifact created at version 0 against the dev environment; backend tests reached 782.

Making a second instance actually see pulled work (v0.66.3–v0.66.5) exposed a cascade of bugs that had all been masked by the permissive local Hub emulator, which echoes the full published payload (so tests and headless acceptance passed) while the real Appian Hub stores only its contract fields.
scope: Lesson: emulator fidelity gaps hide puller-side bugs until a real Hub is used.

statement: In v0.66.3 pull crashed on a not-null title constraint because the Hub stage_artifact record has no title; the upsert now fills every not-null, no-default local column missing from the mirror payload (title from a stage label, timestamps from now) via a required-columns helper.
scope: Lesson/fix: pulled mirror rows must satisfy local not-null columns the Hub does not carry.

statement: Pulled features did not populate the Workbench board because auto-membership requires a non-null stories-finalized timestamp that the Hub feature record drops; board pull now derives that timestamp (a pulled feature with stories was finalized upstream).
scope: Lesson/fix: derive dropped finalized timestamp so pulled features board correctly.

statement: In v0.66.4 completed pulled stages wrongly showed a start-the-stage prompt because the stage page gated the workspace on a chat session id, but a pulled mirror has the artifact with no local chat (chat and runs stay local per ADR-063); a third, read-only branch was added for a completed/in-review chat-less stage (the artifact plus a shared-by-team banner and export).
scope: Lesson/fix: render pulled chat-less stages read-only instead of gating on a local chat session.

statement: In v0.66.5 the derived stage title maps each stage key to a human label via a labels table: spec to Spec, ux_design to UX Design, technical_design to Technical Design, breakdown to Feature Breakdown.
scope: Mapping from stage key to displayed title for pulled stages.

statement: A per-entity probe comparing outbound payload keys to the frozen contract fields confirmed the only genuinely-dropped, non-attribution fields are the feature's stories-finalized timestamp and the stage artifact's title, both correctly derived on the puller; the published-by attribution is not lost because the Hub stores it as created-by/modified-by and the record mapper recovers it.
scope: Probe result establishing which fields the Hub drops and how they are recovered/derived.

statement: Pulled entities are read-only mirrors on the pulling instance, so derived or defaulted values never flow back to the Hub.
scope: Invariant for pulled mirrors on a non-authoring instance.

statement: v0.66.3–v0.66.5 were verified live when a second instance pulled one feature, twelve epics, seventy-two stories and four stage artifacts plus seventy-two board cards with each stage opening read-only; gates passed and regression tests were added for title-less stage pull, board-populate-after-pull, and the read-only pulled-stage view.

Before auto-pull (v0.67.0) a puller only pulled via a manual Sync-now action, so a teammate's board move or feature and story updates did not reflect until a manual sync; the 30-second changes poll only updated the updates-available indicator and never auto-applied.

The auto-pull hook, mounted once in the app shell, pulls automatically on app load, on every route change, on a 30-second interval, and on window refocus or tab-visible; it is throttled (a minimum gap between real pulls plus an in-flight guard), gated on collaboration being enabled and available, and silent on error, and after each pull it invalidates the applications, features, workbench and collab queries.
Auto-applying pulls is safe because pulled entities are read-only mirrors on the pulling instance, so there is no local draft to clobber; notify-then-apply only matters on the authoring instance.
scope: Why background pulls can be applied without confirmation on a puller.

statement: The pull hook gained a quiet option for the background driver; tests cover that it auto-pulls when enabled and available and no-ops when disabled.
scope: Background-driver option and test coverage for auto-pull.

statement: Both fleet instances were restarted on v0.67.0 so that teammate moves reflect within about 30 seconds (or on navigation) with no manual step.

For the v0.67.1 latency fix the root cause was measured before any change: a live probe showed a published story was visible through the changes manifest and a record read in about 0.9 seconds, so there was no Appian replica lag (read-your-writes) and the eventual-consistency hypothesis was wrong; the real delay was the flat 30-second front-end cadence, since the backend had no background pull loop and the KB Hub-pull scheduler is KB-only and off by default.
scope: Lesson: measure the cause (no replica lag; cadence was the delay) before changing sync behaviour.

statement: The v0.67.1 auto-pull became board-aware and event-driven: the interval is 10 seconds while a Workbench board route is open and 30 seconds otherwise, and each tick runs a cheap changes poll that issues a real pull only when the Hub change cursor advances since the last seen value (the first poll just seeds the cursor), avoiding pull-write churn on idle ticks.
Auto-pull force-pulls on app load or window reload (bypassing the throttle) plus a throttled pull on every route change, and refocus or tab-visible also trigger the change-driven check.

With the Hub read at about 0.9 seconds, a teammate board move reflects within about 10 seconds on the board or instantly on reload/navigation; the auto-pull hook gained injectable timing options for testing and a new event-driven test was added.

The v0.68.0 cause was measured from a request log: with Hub read-your-writes at about 0.9 seconds a passive puller made only one request in 45 seconds because browsers throttle or pause background-tab timers (roughly one poll per minute for a hidden tab), so no front-end interval can keep a background tab synced.
scope: Lesson: browser background-tab timer throttling defeats front-end-only sync cadence.

statement: The v0.68.0 fix moved the pull cadence to the backend: a change-gated service tick checks the Hub change manifest against a persisted auto-pull cursor and runs the full pull plus board pull only when the cursor advances (or on the first tick), and is a no-op when collaboration is disabled.

A browser-independent backend auto-puller runs as an always-on 10-second asyncio task started and stopped in the app lifespan, gated live on the enabled check (so the ADR-065 toggle flips without a restart) and ticking off the event loop via to-thread to avoid the blocking-write deadlock lesson, keeping a puller synced regardless of any browser tab.
scope: Backend always-on auto-pull loop must run its blocking work off the event loop.

statement: The board hook gained a 10-second local refetch interval (a cheap local read that React Query pauses while hidden and refetches on focus) so an open board reflects the backend-synced local data.
scope: Local board refresh so the backend auto-pull is visible (v0.68.0).

statement: v0.68.0 was verified live with no browser open: a second instance's local story lane flipped from to-do to code-review about 10 seconds after a board-move publish from the main instance, driven by the backend loop alone.

The sticky board header makes the Workbench page a full-height flex column with the app-name row fixed, the board toolbar/filters row non-shrinking and the board region a flexible min-height-zero area with horizontal lane scroll, and each board column fills height with a non-shrinking lane heading and a vertically scrolling card body, so the app name, filters and lane headings stay fixed while cards scroll.
v0.68.0 added two auto-pull-tick tests (change-gated-and-applies and no-op-when-disabled) bringing backend tests to 786, with web tests at 266, and both fleet instances were restarted.

A live report in v0.69.0 found that importing about six stories of a newly-finalized feature onto a board showed all fifty, mostly stuck in Design, and moves to To Do would not stick, traced to three compounding causes.
scope: Symptom cluster that drove the v0.69.0 Workbench board fixes.

statement: Cause one was that board-membership reconciliation carded every finalized story of the application, and the v0.68.0 backend auto-pull loop re-ran it every about 10 seconds, continuously re-adding cards.
scope: Root cause one of the v0.69.0 board problems.

statement: Cause two was that finalized stories defaulted to the design status (the ADR-060 stage start) and a card's lane equals its status, so cards landed in Design rather than the To Do entry lane.
scope: Root cause two of the v0.69.0 board problems.

statement: Cause three was that the v0.68.0 ten-second board refetch raced the optimistic drag, resyncing the items mirror from a background refetch mid-move so moves flickered or reverted.
scope: Root cause three of the v0.69.0 board problems.

statement: Among the v0.69.0 fixes, fix one made finalizing and creating a story default its status to to-do.
Fix two added a migration introducing an on-board flag column on the stories table, backfilled to 1 for currently-carded stories, which rides the story sync payload.
scope: v0.69.0 schema migration adding explicit board membership.

statement: With explicit shared membership, import sets the on-board flag, removing a card clears it, and reconciliation cards only stories whose flag is set; the import and remove hooks publish the affected stories.

The user-owned Hub story record and its upsert/get/list Web APIs gained an additive on-board field (0 or 1), round-trip verified end to end (import then publish then pull syncs both values), where Appian returns a JSON boolean that is coerced to an integer.
scope: Additive Hub contract field for board membership (user-owned side).

statement: Fix three gates the board mirror resync on the reorder mutation not being pending and no drag in progress.
v0.69.0 bumped the schema version from 19 to 20, passed its gates with CI green, restarted both fleet instances, and remediated the main board by flipping the stuck cards to To Do.
Puller-side remove-propagation was deferred: reconciliation should also delete a card when a teammate clears the on-board flag.

Phase 35 (Collaboration Foundations & Identity) shipped as a single-repo genesis change with ADR-063 accepted, the first of a four-phase team-collaboration program (Foundations, the Genesis Hub Appian app, Hub wire-up, Collaborative SDLC).
Collaboration is opt-in and off by default, so a solo install is unchanged.
scope: Default state of collaboration across the program.

statement: Phase 35 built the local-first to shared-Hub substrate: global identifiers plus concurrency columns, a pluggable transport seam, a self-asserted identity model, and the publish/pull service, all exercised against a local/mock provider with no Appian (the Appian Hub comes in phases 36 and 37).
Migration m0019 is additive, forward-only and idempotent and bumps the schema version from 18 to 19.
m0019 adds a text sync-uuid column (with a one-time uuid4 backfill and a unique index) to the six synced tables.
scope: Global identifier column added by m0019.

statement: m0019 adds the row-version CAS column to the four synced tables that lacked the m0014 column.
m0019 adds owner, team and provenance columns to the top-level entities and an upstream-versions JSON column to the stage tables.
m0019 creates the local-only collaboration tables: a singleton identity table, a teams table, a memberships table and a sync-state table.
scope: Local collaboration tables created by m0019.

statement: The six synced-table store create-paths stamp a sync uuid and reads expose it.
scope: How the sync uuid is populated and read.

statement: The identity module provides an Identity model and a store over the identity table (plus a local team/membership read cache); the canonical username resolves in order from the Appian username, then the memory owner username, then the literal local, defensively falling back on an un-migrated database.
scope: Canonical username resolution order and the identity store.

statement: An actor argument was threaded into every lifecycle transition call site so the m0013 audit rows are attributed, and the memory-owner-username consumers now derive from the canonical username.
scope: Attribution wiring for audit rows and memory ownership.

statement: The provider module defines the runtime-checkable SyncProvider protocol, the provider-neutral DTOs and the HubConflict type, with no Appian dependency.
scope: The transport seam contract and DTOs.

statement: The local Hub provider is a file-backed emulator (the test double) under the configured hub directory offering base-version CAS producing a HubConflict, content-hash blob dedup, a monotonic change-log manifest with a changes-since cursor, advisory markers with TTL, and teams/memberships.
scope: The local provider emulator used for tests.

statement: The service publish maps a row to a payload with the local-only no-leak exclusion, puts the record with a base-version CAS, and then stamps the published provenance locally.
scope: Publish path of the collaboration service.

statement: The service pull walks the manifest from the sync-state cursor and upserts local mirrors keyed by sync uuid with local-only columns null, alongside blob helpers, an advisory heartbeat and an opt-in enabled gate.
scope: Pull path of the collaboration service.

statement: In phase 35 the bindings wire only the feature entity; stories, stages and boards are deferred to phase 38 because they need cross-machine parent resolution.
scope: Which entities were sync-bound as of phase 35.

statement: The content hash is sha256.

The provider factory returns None unless collaboration is enabled and the provider is set to local; settings gained the collaboration enabled, provider and Hub URL values (from the matching environment variables) plus a Hub directory property.

The collaboration API exposes config, identity get/put, team list/create, team join, active-team set and team members endpoints (team routes return 409 when disabled), with the service attached to app state and a Collaboration-identity preflight item shown only when a Hub is configured.

The web adds a Settings Collaboration tab (Hub status/opt-in, identity form, team management shown only when enabled) and a deferrable first-run onboarding dialog mounted in the app shell that appears only when collaboration is enabled and no identity is set.

At the Phase 35 release the gates passed (backend tests and lint, web type-check, lint, unit tests and build) and a two-instance local-provider acceptance script passed all nine checks covering the opt-in gate, canonical username, feature sync uuid, publish, pull mirror with provenance, no-op re-pull and solo fallback.

Phase 35 deliberately left to later phases the Appian Hub app and its Web APIs/record types/blob store (36), the real Appian provider plus KB sharing and live identity/teams (37), and features/artifacts/stories/boards publish-pull plus the collaboration UX and adoption bulk-publish (38), with shared-memory sync deferred.
Per-team visibility is stamped via tags but not enforced, and identity verification / anti-spoofing is parked.
scope: Known limitations: visibility is not enforced and identity is not verified.

statement: Phase 35 released genesis from v0.62.0 to v0.63.0 (bumping the package, web version and app anchors), pushed the tag to master with CI green through a clean install at database version 19, and moved no core/SDK/workflows pins.

Phase 37 (Hub Wire-up) shipped as a single-repo genesis change with no migration (m0019 still stands), implementing the ADR-063 sync-provider seam against the ADR-064 deployed Genesis Hub app, and depends on phase 35 (the collab seam and identity/teams) and phase 36 (the frozen contract and fixtures).
Phase 37 brought the first two shared surfaces (the application KB and identity/teams) live against the real Appian Hub, plus a reusable sync-UX foundation that phase 38 extends.
The real Appian sync provider maps every protocol method onto the frozen Genesis Hub API contract version 1.0.0.
scope: The Appian provider implements the frozen Hub contract v1.0.0.

statement: The Appian provider implements record upsert/get/list with a base-version CAS that returns a HubConflict on a 409, and blob put (dedup returns 200, new returns 201), get and versions.
scope: Record and blob operations of the Appian provider.

statement: The provider implements a changes-since cursor manifest, activity set/list/clear, and teams and memberships as generic record kinds with a deterministic uuid5 membership key.
The Appian API key is resolved from the ADR-048 dev-environment per-environment secret-provider scope and is never logged.
scope: Credential handling for the Appian provider.

statement: The provider transport is injectable and defaults to requests with retry/backoff on 5xx and 429 responses.
scope: HTTP transport behaviour of the Appian provider.

statement: Hub reads are treated as eventually consistent, so the provider trusts the version returned by a put or post and never re-reads the record.
Availability pings the meta endpoint and only warns (never hard-fails) on a contract-version mismatch; the provider is registered under the appian provider name.
The Appian provider's contract conformance is tested against the shared phase-36 fixtures, vendored into the test fixtures directory.

Hydrating the KB from a pulled blob performs an SCD-2 replace-current in a single transaction: it closes all current objects and edges, baseline-opens the pulled snapshot, recomputes bundles, marks the business map stale, and records a hub-pull sync.
scope: KB hydration from a Hub blob.

statement: KB hydration is blocking, so callers must offload it to a worker thread (the checkpointer-deadlock lesson from bible section 7).
scope: Blocking KB hydration must run off the event loop.

statement: The KB blob is a gzipped code-free parse result in the result-json shape, serialized and deserialized through an attribute-shim decoupled from the parser dataclasses, containing no SAIL per ADR-037.
scope: Format of the shared KB blob.

statement: The KB blob gzip is written with a zero modification time so identical content is byte-identical and the Hub content-hash dedup hits.
scope: Determinism requirement for KB blob gzip so dedup works.

statement: Publishing the KB serializes it and puts a KB blob keyed by app uuid with content-hash dedup (no new version if unchanged), while the pull-first path hydrates only when the Hub blob is newer than the local KB cursor (avoiding a needless re-parse); the Hub app itself is excluded by its configured uuid.

The applications API adds a pull endpoint (pull-first) and a publish endpoint (deliberate refresh then publish), rejects the Hub app from add, and reuses the existing sync-busy 409 guard to prevent a double export.

An off-by-default KB Hub-pull scheduler job lets a designated machine run the daily refresh while others pull first, and the app composition builds the collaboration service before the applications and scheduler wiring so they share one instance.
scope: Scheduler wiring for KB Hub pulls.

statement: The collaboration onboarding and Settings identity/team routes are provider-agnostic, so they automatically hit real Appian once the provider is appian, while the local teams and memberships tables remain the offline cache.

A publish with no canonical identity is blocked so there is never a silent unattributed write; the onboarding guard is enforced in both publish and KB publish, and the publish API maps the not-onboarded error to a 409.
scope: No unattributed publishes; onboarding is required.

statement: Onboarding is decided from the locally-cached identity (the canonical username) so it works offline, and the published-by attribution carries the canonical username end to end.

The backend adds an availability check and a changes-since passthrough with a status endpoint and a cursor-parameterized changes endpoint that degrade to empty when disabled or unreachable so the poll no-ops.

Web hooks poll Hub status and changes on an interval only while a relevant view is open, plus a sync-now check-for-updates action, and a Hub-status component shows live reachability with an offline working-locally state and renders nothing when disabled.
scope: Sync-UX web hooks and the status component.

statement: The staleness badge and its pure predicate implement notify-then-apply: it offers a review prompt only when the Hub version is strictly higher and never auto-overwrites.
scope: Staleness notification must never auto-overwrite local data.

statement: An independent auditor confirmed the phase-37 design and reported findings.

A must-fix found that gzip compression embeds the current time on Python 3.13, so identical KB content hashed differently every publish and the Hub dedup never hit; it was fixed with a zero modification time plus a determinism regression test.
scope: Lesson: gzip embeds mtime and breaks content-hash dedup unless pinned.

statement: A should-fix addressed the pull and publish endpoints returning a raw 500 on a down or unauthorized Hub: the transport and auth errors were promoted to the transport-neutral provider module and the endpoints now degrade to 503 when unreachable and 401 on a bad key.
scope: Error mapping hardening for the KB share endpoints.

statement: Minor nits (blob status not surfaced, get-blob latest-only, list-records since, broad offline excepts) were documented or deferred to phase 38, and the deliverable two-instance local-hub acceptance script passed all checks.
scope: Phase 37 audit nits and acceptance deliverable.

statement: Phase 37 released genesis v0.64.0 (three anchors bumped, web bundle rebuilt and committed) with no migration, genesis-only.
At the phase-37 release the gates passed (backend tests and lint, web type-check, lint, unit tests and build), the other four repos were unchanged, and master and the version pipelines ran in CI.

The phase-37 live acceptance (user-driven) deploys the phase-36 Hub, configures Settings Collaboration (base URL and service-account key) on two instances, onboards both, refreshes from Appian on instance A to parse and publish the KB blob, syncs on instance B to pull and hydrate without parsing, and verifies the team and attribution on both; the headless harness proves the same flow against the local provider.

Phase 37 left to phase 38 per-entity publish/pull for features, published stage artifacts, stories/epics and boards (with their per-entity sync-UX wiring) plus the one-time adoption bulk-publish, with shared-memory sync deferred.

Phase 38 (Collaborative SDLC) shipped as a single-repo genesis change with no migration (phase-35 m0019 stands), implementing ADR-063 for the human-authored entities over the phase-37 Appian provider and collaboration service, and is the fourth and final phase of the collaboration program.

Phase 38 made the human-authored SDLC work products (features with published stage artifacts, epics and stories, and boards) sync across the team with the full collaboration UX and a one-time adoption path.
All phase-38 collaboration sync is opt-in and off by default, so a solo install is unchanged.
The whole collaboration mechanism is provider-agnostic and was built and verified against the file-backed local Hub provider; the live Appian Hub is the same interface.
scope: Provider-agnostic design verified against the local provider.

statement: The collaboration service gained cross-machine parent resolution (a parent-ref mapping a local integer foreign key to the parent's global sync uuid) plus artifact-bytes sync.
scope: Cross-machine parent resolution for per-entity sync.

statement: Publishing a feature stage happens on completion: it gates on the completed status, lazily publishes the parent feature, uploads the artifact bytes as an artifact blob, then puts the stage metadata with a base-version CAS.
Local-only fields never reach the Hub: the chat session id, run id, local html path and feature id are excluded via the local-only set and the outbound foreign-key translation.

Pulling a stage produces a read-only mirror: it resolves the parent (skip-and-retry if the parent is not local yet, so the cursor never advances past an unresolved parent), writes the bytes to the puller's own stage-artifacts directory as a pulled html file and points the html path there, and leaves chat and run null.
Stage tables have no published-version column (m0019), so a stage's CAS base is the sync-state cursor keyed by feature-stage and sync uuid.
Epic and story bindings were added; a story's optional nullable epic id stays null and the story is never skipped for a missing parent.

The JSON columns (acceptance criteria, questions, labels) are stored locally as JSON strings but travel as arrays on the wire so the Appian story-item normalization can explode them, and are lossless both ways.
scope: Wire representation of story JSON columns.

statement: Publishing the feature backlog is the Finalize trigger (feature plus epics plus stories); epic and story publishes lazily publish parents; and a deletion publish sends a deleted-tombstone that makes pull remove the mirror.
scope: Backlog publish, lazy parents and deletion tombstone.

statement: A mandatory round-trip fidelity test (a multi-kilobyte unicode/emoji description, twenty long acceptance criteria, empty labels and a null epic) is a release gate.
scope: Release-gate fidelity test for story sync.

statement: A board lane equals the story's status (which rides the already-synced story record), and publishing a board move is a story publish (status and CAS) plus a board-state signal record.
scope: Board lane syncing via story status.

statement: Automatic membership reconciliation adds a card for every shared finalized story of the app on the local board (cross-machine because the pulled feature carries the stories-finalized timestamp), and the board pull drains board-state signals and reconciles all local boards.
scope: Automatic board membership and board pull.

statement: The in-lane board position and which boards you curated stay local and are never published.
scope: Local-only board state that is never shared.

statement: A thin backend action surface exposes publishing a stage (by id and by feature-and-stage), the backlog, a story, a board move and a deletion, plus a pull endpoint, activity get/post/delete by kind, and adopt, with Hub error mapping consistent with phase 37-05 (409/401/503/404; disabled maps to 409; advisory degrades to empty).
scope: Collaboration sync action API and error mapping.

statement: The web adds the API client, hooks and SDLC controls (a publish-to-team button that is publish-on-complete and opt-in gated, a published-by indicator and an advisory marker) reusing the phase-37 Hub-status and staleness-badge components; the publish button mounts in the stage workspace action bar for all four stages, an explicit board lane move auto-publishes best-effort gated on the cached opt-in config, and a sync-now control sits in Settings.
scope: Phase 38 collaboration web controls and mounts.

statement: Adoption preview counts the local completed/finalized work not yet published, and adopt-publish publishes only that work in order (stages, then epics, then stories, then boards).
Adopt-publish is idempotent (a re-run is a no-op), never automatic, requires onboarding, and returns zeros when disabled.
scope: Constraints on the adoption bulk publish.

statement: An adoption preview endpoint and an adopt endpoint back a Settings adoption card that requires a two-step explicit confirm.
The phase-38 independent audit returned a ship verdict with no must-fix findings.
Audit fix C1 made a drag-drop cross-lane move publish only the crossed card while in-lane reorders stay local.
The acceptance script caught that the backlog publish must always re-publish the feature at Finalize so the stories-finalized timestamp propagates.
scope: Lesson: re-publish the feature at finalize so downstream board membership derives correctly.

statement: A should-fix made pull seed each story's board-state CAS cursor so a second contributor's move publishes cleanly, and widened the set-activity guard.
scope: Phase 38 should-fix for second-contributor board moves.

statement: The phase-38 deliverable was a headless full-SDLC hand-off acceptance script (publish, mirror, finalize, boards, adoption, no-leak) that passed all checks.
Phase 38 released genesis v0.65.0 (three anchors bumped, web bundle rebuilt and committed) with no migration, genesis-only.

At the phase-38 release the gates passed (backend tests and lint, web type-check, lint, unit tests and build), the full-SDLC live-acceptance script passed headlessly, and the other four repos were unchanged.

The phase-38 live acceptance deploys the phase-36 Hub, configures Settings Collaboration and onboards two instances to one team, then a product owner publishes a spec, UX auto-sees it and publishes a UX design, a developer picks up technical design then breakdown, Finalize publishes stories, board lanes sync, and attribution and adoption are visible; the acceptance script proves the same flow headless against the local provider.

Two display follow-ups were deferred without blocking ship: per-stage published-by attribution and the cross-stage staleness badge mount, both constrained by the no-migration rule because the stage table has no published-by or published-version column (attribution and staleness are available on features, stories and boards, which carry the columns); carried as a post-release UI follow-up with options A1/A2/B1.

The local-first plus shared-Hub collaboration program is delivered for the KB (phase 37) and features/artifacts, stories and boards (phase 38), with shared-memory sync the one remaining deferred future phase.

The phase-35 spec shipped with ADR-063 accepted at genesis v0.63.0; it is a single-repo genesis change, the first of four collaboration phases, and depends on several prior ADRs (local single-user, DB-agnostic repositories, the provider-interface precedents, per-environment Appian credentials, shared memory scope, the lifecycle service/audit/CAS, and the finalized epics/stories/board).

Genesis is a local single-user app where all data lives only in the user's local database, which suits a solo engineer but prevents a team working the same Appian application from collaborating (each developer re-parses the same app, a finished spec is invisible to others, and a board's status is private to one machine).

Genesis stays local-first but lets a team selectively centralize a defined subset of data to a shared Collaboration Hub: the shared entities are the application KB, features with their published stage artifacts, stories/epics and board status, while chat, runs, the installed workflow catalog, documents and personal memory stay local-only (shared memory deferred).

Collaboration is impossible without identity: you cannot record who published or last updated something, attribute a lifecycle transition, or scope a team without a per-user identity, which Genesis lacked (the lifecycle actor was always null and the memory owner username was an unused config string).

This phase builds the substrate the other three phases plug into: the pluggable sync-provider seam, global identifiers on every entity that will sync, a user and team identity model with onboarding and a Settings page, and a publish/pull service with a local/mock provider so the whole mechanism is buildable and shippable before the Appian Hub exists; everything is opt-in and off by default.

Goal one is a pluggable collaboration seam providing a sync-provider protocol with the record, blob, change-manifest and advisory-lock operations publish/pull needs plus a provider registry, with a collaboration service owning the transport-agnostic publish/pull logic and a local/mock provider as the first implementation.

Goal two adds a stable client-generated sync uuid to every entity that will sync (and backfills existing rows) plus a row-version column on the synced tables that lack it, so an entity created on one machine can be referenced unambiguously on another (local integer primary keys collide across machines).

Goal three is a user and team identity model: onboarding captures the user's self-asserted name, Appian username and email and their team, with the Appian username as the single canonical user id used everywhere, and teams and membership as UUID-keyed Hub entities captured and cached locally so attribution works offline.
Goal four is a Settings page to manage identity and team plus the first-run onboarding UI and the Hub-configuration / opt-in UI.

Goal five is the provenance, versioning and advisory-lock plumbing: every shared entity carries a version plus published-by and published-at, a stage records which upstream artifact versions it consumed (for the notify-only cross-stage staleness badge), and a soft in-progress advisory marker with heartbeat/TTL rides the provider, backed by the row-version CAS as the correctness safety net.

Goal six is opt-in and off by default: the entire collaboration layer is gated behind a feature flag plus Hub configuration, and with no Hub configured Genesis behaves exactly as today (solo, offline, no identity requirement), with the global-ids migration additive and harmless for solo users.

Success means that with collaboration enabled against the local/mock provider a developer completes onboarding, the app stamps their canonical username on transitions and edits, every syncable entity has a stable sync uuid, and the service can publish an entity or blob to the mock Hub and pull it back on a second simulated instance, while a solo user with no Hub configured sees zero change.

Locked decision 1: local-first is preserved; Genesis stays a local single-user app that works fully offline and solo, and the Hub is opt-in for only a defined subset of data, so ADR-063 amends ADR-026 rather than reversing it.

Locked decision 2: shared data is the application KB, features with published stage artifacts, stories/epics and boards; local-only data is chat, runs, catalog, documents and personal memory; shared memory is deferred to a later phase.
Locked decision 3: the Hub is the team's Appian dev environment (the environment Genesis already syncs), which doubles as the Hub, so there is no separate Hub environment.
scope: Locked with the user 2026-09-05; the Appian side is phase 36.

statement: Locked decision 4: identity is self-asserted at onboarding (name, Appian username and email) and Appian is not an identity provider (no whoami or authentication against it); the Appian username is the canonical user id for published-by/modified-by, the lifecycle actor and the personal-memory owner, with spoofing and typo hardening parked.
Locked decision 5: teams are a Genesis-owned entity (not Appian groups), UUID-keyed with client-generated ids, stored in the Hub and visible to all.

Locked decision 6: visibility is open for now (everyone can see everyone's applications, features, stories and boards), but an owner and team uuid are stamped on shared entities as a forward-compatible seam for per-team visibility later (tagged now, not enforced).

Locked decision 7: a shared service account writes to the Hub (phase 37) and attribution comes from the payload Genesis sends (created-by/modified-by equal to the acting user's canonical username), not from Appian's auth context.

Locked decision 8: concurrency is a soft advisory in-progress marker (heartbeat/TTL, cleared on publish or when stale) to prevent accidental double-work, plus the existing row-version CAS raising a stale-write error to guarantee no silent overwrite even if the advisory is ignored; there is no hard lock.
Locked decision 9: opt-in and off by default, so no Hub configured means Genesis is unchanged (solo, offline, no identity gate), and the sync-uuid migration is additive and safe for solo installs.

Locked decision 10: global identifiers are mandatory groundwork, so synced entities get a stable sync uuid and the migration backfills existing rows, while local integer primary keys stay as an additional key with a local-to-global map on hydrate.

The entities that will sync all used local integer-autoincrement primary keys and local integer foreign keys (which collide across machines), and the row-version column existed on the stage and story tables via the m0014 pattern but not on features, epics, board cards or boards, where this phase adds it.
scope: Code-grounded current state of synced tables.

statement: The local-only linkages are already foreign-key-free independent-lifecycle columns (chat session id, run id, html path, source doc path), which is what makes artifact bytes move while chat and runs stay local: the sync payload publishes the artifact content, status and hash and leaves the local-only columns null on the puller.
scope: Why local-only artifact columns enable clean sync.

statement: The provider-interface precedent is real in the agent-provider and document-provider registries, and the sync-provider mirrors that shape.

Identity was unwired before this phase: the lifecycle event accepts a username but every transition call site passed no actor so all m0013 audit rows were unattributed, and the memory owner username was a config string rather than a real identity; this phase introduces the identity and threads it into the transition actor argument.

Repositories are DB-agnostic: stores take a Database, never open ad-hoc connections, and never create tables (the schema is owned by the migrations directory), and the new migration and collab package follow that pattern.

The app composition root registers routes, so the new collab, onboarding and settings routes register there; the web is React/TypeScript with a Settings tabs shell, query hooks, API prefixing and design tokens; overall the phase is one additive migration plus the new collab package, onboarding, a Settings identity/team page and the opt-in flag, with no Appian and no other repo.

Migration m0019 (collab_identity_and_sync_ids) adds a unique text sync uuid (backfilled) and a not-null-default-zero integer row version to the listed tables, plus owner-username and team-uuid tags (stamped, not enforced) on the top-level synced entities and published-by/published-at/published-version provenance columns.

m0019 adds a local singleton identity table holding the user's name, Appian username, email and active team uuid, local teams and memberships tables that are a read cache of Hub-authored data, and a sync-state table holding per-entity-kind pull cursors and last-published-version markers for the change-manifest and pull-if-newer logic.
The chat, runs, documents and memory tables are unchanged (they stay local-only), and the exact DDL, sync-uuid backfill and store read/write changes are locked in sub-specs 35-01 and 35-02.

The sync-provider record operations are a put-record taking kind, sync uuid, payload and a keyword base-version and returning a put-result (a version CAS raising a stale-write-equivalent conflict), a get-record by kind and sync uuid, and a list-records by kind with an optional since.
The sync-provider blob operations are a put-blob taking kind, key, bytes and keyword content-hash and meta and returning a blob-ref, a get-blob by ref, and a list-blob-versions by kind and key.
exact: put_blob(kind, key, bytes, *, content_hash, meta) -> BlobRef

statement: The sync-provider change manifest is a changes-since taking a cursor and returning the changes and a next cursor (the small what's-new feed).
The sync-provider advisory-lock operations are a set-activity taking kind, sync uuid, username and a keyword ttl, a clear-activity and a list-activity.
The sync-provider identity and team operations are upsert-team, list-teams, upsert-membership, list-memberships and resolve-user by username.

The collaboration service owns the transport-agnostic publish/pull orchestration (per-kind entity-record mapping, version and provenance stamping, base-version-CAS conflict detection with notify-then-apply, change-manifest pull decisions and the advisory-lock heartbeat) and depends only on the sync-provider protocol, never on Appian.

The local Hub provider is a file-backed in-process emulator (records, blobs, manifest and activity under a local directory) and the test double, and the provider registry is keyed by provider type (local now, appian in phase 37) and returns none (collaboration disabled) when no Hub is configured.

The identity module holds the local identity model and a current-user accessor reading the cached profile; the Appian username is canonical and the memory owner username becomes a derived read of it, and attribution is threaded by passing the current user's username as the transition actor and carrying created-by/modified-by/published-by on publish payloads from the same source, finally populating the m0013 audit seam.
Onboarding is a first-run readiness item required before the first publish, not before using Genesis.
Teams are created client-side with a UUID so creation works offline and never collides, are upserted to the provider, and are mirrored in a local cache.

The web delivers a first-run onboarding flow (only when collaboration is enabled: confirm identity, pick or create a team) and a Settings identity/team page (view/edit the local profile, see the active team and members, switch/join/create a team, and the Hub configuration plus opt-in toggle), all against the mock provider this phase and repointed at the Appian provider in phase 37, using design tokens, the API client, query hooks, accessibility tests and a committed web bundle.
scope: Phase 35 web onboarding and Settings page.

statement: ADR-063 (accepted, phase 35, genesis v0.63.0): Genesis stays a local-first single-user app but gains an opt-in capability to selectively centralize a defined subset of data (application KB, features with published stage artifacts, stories/epics and boards, but not chat/runs/catalog/documents/personal-memory) to a shared Collaboration Hub via a pluggable sync-provider seam, with publish-on-complete plus pull; data is keyed by stable sync uuids, concurrency is optimistic row-version CAS plus a soft advisory marker with no hard lock, cross-stage dependency staleness is notify-only with provenance, identity is self-asserted with the Appian username canonical, teams are Genesis-owned UUID-keyed Hub entities, and visibility is open with owner and team uuid stamped for a future scoping seam; it amends ADR-026, relates to ADR-030/048/053, and the concrete Appian Hub backend and contract is ADR-064.
scope: The ADR-063 decision as stated in the phase-35 spec (authoritative copy also in the decision log).

statement: ADR-063 pull modes: pull is automatic for read-only shared views and boards, notify-then-apply where a local draft exists, and available manually via a sync-now action.
scope: How pulls are applied under ADR-063.

statement: The phase-35 release is single-repo genesis with no core/SDK/workflows pin moves; each sub-phase runs build, gates, local commit, independent review and docs with no tag or push until the release sub-phase on the user's go-ahead, and the clean-install CI job must migrate a fresh database to version 19 and serve while the sync-uuid backfill must run correctly on a populated database.
A schema version bump breaks every test that hardcodes the previous current-version, so those tests must be bumped together with the migration.
scope: Lesson applied whenever the schema version changes.

statement: In scope for phase 35 is the m0019 migration, the collab package (seam, service, local/mock provider and registry), the identity/team model with canonical-username unification and actor threading, onboarding, the Settings identity/team and Hub-config opt-in page and the provenance/advisory plumbing, all against the local/mock provider; out of scope to later phases are the Appian Hub app (36), the real Appian provider and KB sharing and live identity/teams (37), per-entity publish-pull and the collaboration UX and adoption (38), shared-memory sync, per-team visibility enforcement (stamped not enforced) and identity verification/anti-spoofing (parked).

There were no blocking open questions (the design forks were resolved with the user on 2026-09-05); deferred to sub-spec 35-01 were the exact m0019 column names, the local collab-table shapes and the sync-provider method signatures.

The phase-35 sub-phase ledger runs linearly: 35-01 data model, sync seam and ADR-063 (docs only); 35-02 the global-identifier and concurrency migration to version 19; 35-03 identity, onboarding and the canonical username; 35-04 the sync-provider seam, service and local provider; 35-05 the web onboarding and Settings page; 35-06 code review and hardening; 35-07 release.
